data.abstract: This project addresses the urgent need to strengthen K–12 teachers’ digital pedagogy by proposing an evidence-based teacher professional development (TPD) framework powered by learning analytics and generative AI. We will (1) develop a teacher practice representation system using multimodal classroom/online learning traces, (2) design an explainable AI reflection and instructional improvement assistant that provides evidence cues, peer benchmarking, and context-aware recommendations, and (3) establish a closed-loop TPD model (data–diagnosis–intervention–evaluation). Using design-based research combined with randomized/quasi-experimental studies in partner schools, we will test mechanisms and impacts on teachers’ TPACK, lesson design quality, classroom interaction patterns, and student learning outcomes. Expected outputs include reusable data dictionaries and indicators, an AI-assisted tool prototype with open components, validated TPD intervention packages and implementation guidelines, high-quality publications, and actionable policy recommendations to support scalable digital transformation in education.

Other-source funds (15.0) will be provided by collaborating units to support additional school training sessions, co-supervision activities, and local infrastructure; these funds do not duplicate NSFC direct costs.

proposal_body.innovation_ideas_and_key_research_clues_: Key clue: combine interpretable learning analytics indicators with a generative-AI coaching interface so that recommendations are grounded in evidence traces and aligned with pedagogical goals; develop a closed-loop TPD model with measurable causal pathways from teacher reflection to classroom interaction to student outcomes.

project_basis_and_research_content.project_rationale: Teacher professional development often lacks timely, context-specific feedback grounded in classroom evidence. Meanwhile, generative AI can provide scalable support but risks hallucination and misalignment with pedagogy if not anchored to trustworthy data. This project bridges the gap by integrating learning analytics with explainable generative AI to support evidence-based digital pedagogy improvements in authentic school contexts.
project_basis_and_research_content.research_content_and_objectives: Content: (1) Build a teacher practice analytics framework: data sources, indicators, and representation of digital pedagogy behaviors; (2) Develop an explainable AI coaching assistant that uses evidence snippets (analytics dashboards, interaction graphs, rubric-aligned indicators) to generate reflective prompts and improvement suggestions; (3) Design and validate a closed-loop TPD intervention (workshops + in-situ coaching + AI-supported reflection); (4) Evaluate effectiveness and mechanisms through iterative pilots and controlled studies. Objectives: improve teachers’ TPACK and lesson design quality; enhance classroom interaction quality; provide scalable, ethical, and generalizable TPD resources.
project_basis_and_research_content.key_scientific_problems: (1) Valid representation: how to reliably represent complex teaching practices from heterogeneous classroom and platform traces; (2) Evidence-grounded generation: how to constrain generative AI outputs with interpretable indicators and provenance to ensure pedagogical validity; (3) Mechanism identification: how changes in reflective practice mediate effects on teaching behaviors and student learning; (4) Generalizability: how to transfer models across subjects, schools, and cultural contexts while respecting privacy and ethics.

project_basic_information.notes_description: International cooperation; emphasis on reproducible measurement workflows and instrument calibration traceability.
project_basic_information.research_direction: Develop automated, calibration-traceable workflows combining FTIR/Raman, DSC, DMA, and microscopy for polymer composite interface assessment, and build interpretable models linking process/chemistry to interfacial performance for robust QC.
project_basic_information.keywords: polymer composites; interface; laboratory automation; calibration and traceability; quality control; multimodal data fusion

data.abstract: Interfacial defects in polymer composites (e.g., poor wetting, incomplete cure, contamination) are a dominant source of performance variability and premature failure. However, current characterization workflows often lack standardization in sample handling, instrument calibration, and data processing, leading to limited reproducibility and delayed quality control (QC) actions. This project will develop an integrated framework that combines multimodal characterization, automated acquisition, calibration traceability, data fusion, and interpretable modeling for robust interface assessment and industrial QC. Key tasks include: (1) implementing automated measurement scripts and LIMS-ready data pipelines for FTIR/Raman, DSC, DMA, and microscopy with full sample/parameter provenance; (2) establishing calibration and drift-monitoring procedures with quantified uncertainty budgets; (3) developing multimodal feature fusion and interpretable models (e.g., sparse regression and tree-based methods) to predict interfacial shear strength and durability, translating outputs into actionable process and inspection thresholds; and (4) validating the approach on representative epoxy/carbon-fiber and thermoplastic composite systems, delivering transferable SOPs for QC automation. Expected outputs include reusable workflow templates and data dictionaries, 2–3 publications or conference papers, and a deployable QC automation solution to improve composite reliability and testing efficiency.

proposal_body.innovation_ideas_and_key_research_clues_: Hypothesis: A calibration-traceable, automated multimodal workflow can reduce inter-lab variability in polymer composite interface metrics by >30% while improving defect detection sensitivity through interpretable data fusion. Key clue: drift and operator-dependent preprocessing dominate variance; controlling provenance + uncertainty enables reliable models and actionable QC thresholds.

project_basis_and_research_content.project_rationale: Industrial composite testing labs often rely on skilled operators and fragmented data handling. Interface-related failures are difficult to diagnose because chemical, thermal, and mechanical indicators are measured separately and rarely fused with process metadata. This project targets reproducibility and decision-making speed by building automated acquisition and traceability, then integrating measurements into interpretable models for QC.
project_basis_and_research_content.research_content_and_objectives: (1) Build automated acquisition and LIMS-ready pipelines for FTIR/Raman, DSC, DMA, and microscopy with standardized metadata, sample IDs, and versioned preprocessing. (2) Implement calibration, drift monitoring, and uncertainty budgets for each modality; define acceptance criteria and periodic checks. (3) Develop multimodal feature sets and interpretable models linking measurements to interfacial performance (e.g., lap shear/interlaminar shear proxies and durability aging outcomes). (4) Validate on epoxy/carbon-fiber and thermoplastic composite panels with controlled defects (contamination, under/over-cure, surface treatment variation) and deliver SOPs and QC thresholds.
project_basis_and_research_content.key_scientific_problems: (a) Quantifying and controlling measurement uncertainty across heterogeneous instruments and operators. (b) Aligning multimodal signals to a shared representation while preserving physical interpretability. (c) Distinguishing true interface degradation signatures from confounders (thickness variation, surface roughness, baseline drift).
project_basis_and_research_content.research_plan_and_feasibility: Year 1: establish data schema, automation scripts, and calibration plans; run repeatability/reproducibility studies and drift characterization. Year 2: generate controlled-defect datasets; implement feature extraction and fusion; develop baseline interpretable models and uncertainty-aware thresholds. Year 3: cross-site validation with cooperating institution; finalize SOPs, documentation, and a deployable QC dashboard prototype. Feasibility is supported by applicant’s daily role in instrumentation calibration and QC investigations and access to routine composite testing infrastructure.
project_basis_and_research_content.features_and_innovations: (1) End-to-end provenance: automated capture of instrument settings, calibration status, and preprocessing versions. (2) Uncertainty-first QC: explicit uncertainty budgets and drift alarms integrated into acceptance criteria. (3) Interpretable multimodal fusion: models that map to physical indicators (cure index, functional group ratios, viscoelastic transitions) rather than black-box outputs. (4) Transferable SOP package designed for industrial labs.
project_basis_and_research_content.annual_research_plan_and_expected_result: Year 1 (2026-09 to 2027-08): automation + calibration SOPs; R&R study report; initial dataset and data dictionary. Year 2 (2027-09 to 2028-08): defect library, fused feature set, first model + QC thresholds; 1 manuscript/technical report. Year 3 (2028-09 to 2029-08): cross-site validation, finalized SOPs and dashboard; 1–2 publications and a best-practice guideline for interface QC.

project_basic_information.research_direction: Design, modeling, and evaluation of AI-driven adaptive feedback and learning analytics to improve adult learners’ skill acquisition and transfer in workplace upskilling programs
project_basic_information.keywords: adult learning; workplace upskilling; generative AI; adaptive feedback; learning analytics

data.abstract:
This project investigates how AI-supported adaptive feedback influences adult learners’ engagement, learning strategies, skill mastery, and transfer in workplace upskilling contexts. Integrating learning sciences and educational technology, we will develop an interpretable model for generating and regulating feedback under constraints such as task difficulty, prior knowledge, learning goals, and workplace context. The system will produce multi-layer feedback (hints, worked examples, error-specific guidance, and reflection prompts) and use learning analytics to evaluate feedback quality and learning processes in near real time.

The research proceeds in three phases: (1) needs analysis and mechanism modeling using interviews, surveys, and log analysis in enterprise training and continuing education courses; (2) model and system implementation with privacy-preserving data pipelines and an interpretable feedback strategy library, coupled with a causal inference framework linking feedback, behaviors, and outcomes; and (3) multi-context empirical validation via randomized controlled trials and longitudinal follow-ups in digital skills and management training to assess learning gains, transfer, and fairness across learner subgroups. Expected outputs include a mechanism model of adaptive feedback for adult learning, reusable feedback strategies and evaluation metrics, an open-source prototype toolkit, and peer-reviewed publications, supporting lifelong learning and workforce development in China.

Business costs (12.0): field study travel between Beijing/Nanjing and enterprise training sites, participant recruitment and compensation, printing and survey administration, and conference registration for dissemination. Labor costs (15.0): research assistant allowances for data cleaning, annotation of feedback quality, experiment operation, and software prototyping support. Remaining direct costs cover data processing services and software licenses within institutional procurement rules.

Other source funds 5.0 (10k RMB) will be provided by the host lab/enterprise partners as in-kind support and limited cash support for additional participant incentives and platform hosting, ensuring the project can complete multi-site RCTs and longitudinal follow-ups.

proposal_body.innovation_ideas_and_key_research_clues_: Key clue: adult learners’ time constraints and goal-oriented motivation change how feedback is perceived and acted upon; AI feedback must be adaptive not only to knowledge state but also to workplace constraints and transfer demands. Innovation: an interpretable, privacy-preserving adaptive feedback framework that connects feedback generation strategies with causal evidence of learning and transfer outcomes.

project_basis_and_research_content.project_rationale: Workplace upskilling is critical for economic transformation and lifelong learning. Adult learners often face fragmented study time, high performance pressure, and heterogeneous prior knowledge. Generative AI offers scalable feedback, but current applications frequently lack pedagogical grounding, interpretability, and rigorous evidence in authentic adult learning settings. This project addresses the need for mechanism-based, evidence-driven adaptive feedback that improves learning efficiency and transfer while ensuring fairness and privacy.
project_basis_and_research_content.research_content_and_objectives:
Content: (1) characterize adult learners’ feedback needs and constraints in workplace courses; (2) build an interpretable adaptive feedback strategy model combining learner state, task features, and contextual constraints; (3) develop a prototype system that delivers multi-layer feedback and records interaction traces; (4) evaluate effectiveness, transfer, and fairness via RCTs and longitudinal follow-up.
Objectives: (a) propose a mechanism model explaining how adaptive feedback affects engagement, strategy use, and transfer; (b) produce a reusable feedback strategy library and measurement framework; (c) demonstrate measurable improvements in learning gains and transfer compared with non-adaptive or generic AI feedback; (d) provide practical guidelines for enterprise training providers.
project_basis_and_research_content.key_scientific_problems:
1) Mechanism identification: what mediates the effect of AI feedback on adult learners (e.g., cognitive load, self-efficacy, metacognitive monitoring) under time constraints?
2) Adaptation under constraints: how to adapt feedback to knowledge state and workplace context while maintaining interpretability and avoiding hallucination or over-assistance?
3) Causal evaluation: how to estimate causal effects of different feedback strategies using learning logs with selection bias and heterogeneous treatment effects?
4) Fairness and privacy: how to ensure comparable benefits across age/experience groups while protecting sensitive workplace data?
project_basis_and_research_content.research_plan_and_feasibility:
Plan: Year 1—needs analysis, instrument development, baseline data collection, and initial mechanism model; build privacy-preserving data pipeline and feedback taxonomy. Year 2—develop adaptive feedback strategy library and prototype; pilot studies to refine prompts, guardrails, and measurement; preregister evaluation protocols. Year 3—multi-site RCTs in at least two course types (digital skills, management/communication); collect longitudinal follow-up data for transfer; finalize causal models and practical guidelines.
Feasibility: Applicant has industry experience in corporate training and e-learning project management, enabling access to training providers and realistic task design. Host institution provides methodological support, computing resources, and ethics oversight. Cooperating institution supports evaluation design and adult learning theory integration.
project_basis_and_research_content.features_and_innovations:
1) Adult-learning-centered adaptive feedback model integrating workplace constraints (time, goals, performance pressure) with learning state.
2) Interpretable feedback strategy library with explicit rules/conditions and traceable rationale.
3) Privacy-preserving learning analytics pipeline for enterprise contexts.
4) Causal inference framework linking feedback strategies to behaviors and outcomes, enabling evidence-based optimization.
5) Comprehensive evaluation including transfer and fairness across learner subgroups.
project_basis_and_research_content.annual_research_plan_and_expected_result:

project_basic_information.notes_description: Focus on scalable community surveillance and data quality; includes capacity building for field teams and ethical data governance.
project_basic_information.research_direction: Develop and evaluate an integrated community-based NCD surveillance model combining digital reporting, standardized indicators, and implementation strategies within primary care catchment areas.
project_basic_information.keywords: non-communicable diseases; community surveillance; digital health; data quality; implementation science

data.abstract: This project will develop and evaluate a community-based surveillance system for non-communicable diseases (hypertension, diabetes, and related risk factors) across multiple neighborhoods in Santo Domingo. The study will integrate primary care catchment activities with community outreach using mobile digital reporting, standardized indicators, and a structured data quality assurance workflow. Guided by implementation science, we will identify barriers and facilitators affecting data collection, reporting, and feedback loops. The work will proceed in three phases: (1) baseline needs assessment and consensus on indicators; (2) development and pilot testing of digital tools and a training package; and (3) scale-up and evaluation across several primary care areas. Primary outcomes include data completeness, timeliness, and consistency; field team adherence to protocols; community participation; and usability of outputs for policy and program decisions. Deliverables will include a replicable implementation package (tools, SOPs, training materials, and an ethical data governance plan) to strengthen urban NCD prevention and support evidence-informed public health policy.

(2) Business costs (42.0): local travel to multiple primary care catchment areas, community meeting logistics, printing of consent and training materials, communication costs, and limited software/service fees for secure data collection and hosting. (3) Labor (50.0): partial support for project coordination, data management, field supervision, and short-term enumerator stipends during baseline and follow-up rounds. Other-source funds (20.0 x10k RMB) from the host institution will co-finance office space, routine utilities, and partial staff time, ensuring feasibility and sustainability.

proposal_body.innovation_ideas_and_key_research_clues_: This proposal combines implementation science with practical digital reporting to close the gap between community-level NCD risk detection and actionable primary-care/public-health decision-making. Key clues: persistent delays/inconsistencies in community NCD data; variable adherence to protocols across sites; and limited feedback loops to frontline teams. The project will test a standardized indicator set, a digital tool with built-in validation, and an implementation package tailored to urban neighborhoods.

project_basis_and_research_content.project_rationale: Urban communities in Santo Domingo face a growing burden of hypertension and diabetes, yet community-level surveillance is fragmented and often paper-based, limiting timeliness and data quality. Strengthening surveillance is essential for targeted prevention, resource allocation, and evaluation of interventions. As a research institute coordinating multi-site studies, we have observed recurring operational bottlenecks (training variability, inconsistent definitions, delayed reporting, and weak feedback). A scalable, ethics-centered, digitally enabled surveillance model is needed to generate reliable evidence for policy and program decisions.
project_basis_and_research_content.research_content_and_objectives: Content: (1) Stakeholder mapping and baseline assessment of current NCD community reporting workflows; (2) consensus on a minimum indicator set and SOPs aligned with primary care needs; (3) design and deployment of a mobile reporting tool with validation rules and audit trails; (4) training and supportive supervision model for field teams; (5) implementation evaluation (reach, adoption, fidelity, acceptability) and effectiveness evaluation (data quality and timeliness). Objectives: O1 establish standardized indicators and governance; O2 improve completeness, timeliness, and consistency of community NCD reports; O3 identify implementation determinants and refine strategies; O4 produce a replication toolkit for scale-up.
project_basis_and_research_content.key_scientific_problems: Problem 1: How to operationalize standardized NCD indicators at the community level while maintaining feasibility for field teams. Problem 2: How to improve data quality (completeness, timeliness, internal consistency) through digital validation and supervision without increasing burden. Problem 3: Which implementation strategies (training intensity, feedback frequency, supervision modality) most influence adoption and fidelity across heterogeneous neighborhoods. Problem 4: How to ensure ethical data governance (consent pathways, minimal data collection, access control) in community surveillance settings.
project_basis_and_research_content.research_plan_and_feasibility: Plan: Year 1—baseline workflow assessment, indicator/SOP consensus, ethics review, prototype development and pilot in 1–2 catchment areas. Year 2—scale to additional sites; implement training, supportive supervision, and monthly feedback dashboards; midline evaluation and iterative improvements. Year 3—endline evaluation; cost and sustainability assessment; dissemination to health authorities and community stakeholders; finalize toolkit. Feasibility: The host institute has established relationships with primary care centers and community leaders, experience coordinating multi-site fieldwork, and existing ethics oversight processes. The applicant’s role in coordinating studies and reporting provides operational capacity to manage data quality and compliance across sites.
project_basis_and_research_content.features_and_innovations: Innovation 1: A pragmatic, standardized indicator set co-designed with frontline primary care and community stakeholders. Innovation 2: Digital reporting with embedded validation, audit trails, and near-real-time dashboards for feedback loops. Innovation 3: Implementation science-driven adaptation using structured measurement of adoption, fidelity, and acceptability to optimize scale-up. Innovation 4: Ethics-by-design governance package (role-based access, minimal dataset, training on consent and confidentiality).
project_basis_and_research_content.annual_research_plan_and_expected_result: Year 1 (2026-07 to 2027-06): baseline assessment report; agreed indicator set and SOPs; pilot-tested digital tool; training curriculum; ethics approvals. Year 2 (2027-07 to 2028-06): expanded implementation across multiple catchment areas; improved data completeness and timeliness versus baseline; implementation determinants analysis; midline policy brief. Year 3 (2028-07 to 2029-06): final effectiveness and implementation evaluation; sustainability/costing summary; open (non-identifiable) aggregated dataset and documentation; replication toolkit and dissemination workshops; manuscripts and policy recommendations.

The host institute has experience with community surveys and collaborative work with academic partners (e.g., UNIBE). Prior internal projects have highlighted gaps in routine NCD reporting that this project will address, and preliminary stakeholder discussions indicate strong interest in standardized digital workflows.
research_foundation_and_work_conditions.work_conditions: Host institute provides office space, secure storage, internet connectivity, and administrative support for procurement and contracting. Field operations will be supported through existing relationships with primary care centers and community organizations in Santo Domingo. Data management will use encrypted devices and controlled-access servers; team members will complete confidentiality and human-subjects protection training.
research_foundation_and_work_conditions.ongoing_related_projects: Ongoing institute activities include routine support to Ministry of Health monitoring initiatives and separate externally funded studies on community health behaviors (non-overlapping data collection instruments). No ongoing project duplicates the proposed digital surveillance system; coordination will ensure shared field logistics do not compromise protocol fidelity.

project_basic_information.research_direction: Comparative analysis of social policy interventions and inequality outcomes; mechanisms of policy implementation at the community level; participatory knowledge translation.
project_basic_information.keywords: social policy; inequality; community-based participatory research; comparative research; knowledge translation

data.abstract: This project conducts a comparative study of urban communities in Canada and China to examine how social policy is implemented at the community level and how implementation pathways shape inequality outcomes related to income security, housing, and social inclusion. The study uses a mixed-methods design: (1) co-developing a cross-national indicator framework and harmonizing publicly available statistics with community-level administrative sources where feasible; (2) conducting stratified community surveys and in-depth interviews in selected sites in both countries; and (3) partnering with nonprofit organizations to run participatory research activities and policy co-design workshops to create a traceable evidence-to-action feedback loop. Expected outputs include a comparative framework and data dictionary, reusable community survey instruments, at least six peer-reviewed English publications and policy briefs, and a practice-oriented guide for government and nonprofit stakeholders. The project will provide new empirical evidence on the mechanisms through which community organizations and service networks mediate policy effects on inequality, while strengthening actionable knowledge translation.

proposal_body.innovation_ideas_and_key_research_clues_: Innovation: linking community-based participatory research (CBPR) with a harmonized comparative policy-implementation dataset to identify mechanisms (service network density, nonprofit intermediation, and administrative discretion) through which policies translate into inequality outcomes. Key clue: policy effects vary less by formal program design than by community-level implementation capacity and relational infrastructure.

project_basis_and_research_content.project_rationale: Persistent inequality in housing stability, income security, and social inclusion remains a major challenge in both Canada and China. While social policies are often evaluated at the program level, less is known about how community-level implementation—through frontline discretion, service networks, and nonprofit partnerships—shapes heterogeneous outcomes. A comparative design allows identification of shared mechanisms and context-specific pathways, improving both theory and practical policy translation.
project_basis_and_research_content.research_content_and_objectives: Content includes: (1) mapping policy implementation ecosystems in selected urban communities (service providers, referral pathways, funding streams); (2) harmonizing comparable indicators of inequality outcomes and local service capacity; (3) conducting community surveys and semi-structured interviews with residents, frontline workers, and nonprofit leaders; (4) participatory co-design workshops to convert findings into actionable recommendations. Objectives: produce a comparative implementation framework; estimate associations between implementation capacity and inequality outcomes; identify mechanisms via qualitative process tracing; and generate policy-relevant tools and briefs for stakeholders.
project_basis_and_research_content.key_scientific_problems: 1) How can community-level policy implementation capacity be operationalized in a cross-nationally comparable way? 2) Through what mechanisms do nonprofit organizations and service networks mediate policy effects on inequality outcomes? 3) How do administrative discretion and local governance arrangements generate heterogeneous impacts within the same policy regime? 4) What knowledge-translation processes most effectively convert evidence into practice in community settings?
project_basis_and_research_content.research_plan_and_feasibility: Year 1: finalize comparative framework; ethics approvals at UBC and cooperating institution; instrument translation/back-translation; pilot in one community per country; build data dictionary and reproducible pipeline. Year 2: full data collection (surveys, interviews, organizational network mapping); preliminary analyses; midterm workshop to validate findings with partners. Year 3: integrated mixed-methods synthesis; policy co-design workshops; finalize publications, briefs, and open protocols. Feasibility: applicant has extensive experience in CBPR, survey design, and mixed methods; host institutions provide research support and established community partnerships; data management plan includes secure storage and de-identification procedures.
project_basis_and_research_content.features_and_innovations: (1) Comparative CBPR methodology with standardized instruments enabling replication; (2) integration of organizational network measures with resident-level outcomes; (3) explicit evidence-to-action feedback loop through co-design workshops; (4) open research outputs (protocols, codebooks, anonymized instruments) to improve transparency and reuse.
project_basis_and_research_content.annual_research_plan_and_expected_result: 2026-09 to 2027-08: framework, ethics, pilots; outputs: protocol, indicator framework, pilot report (1 working paper). 2027-09 to 2028-08: main fieldwork and harmonized dataset; outputs: 2 conference papers, preliminary comparative analysis report, stakeholder brief #1. 2028-09 to 2029-08: synthesis and dissemination; outputs: at least 6 journal articles (planned), stakeholder briefs #2-#3, practice guide, final dataset documentation and instruments.

The team has experience with mixed-methods designs, survey implementation, qualitative coding, and policy-oriented dissemination. The cooperating institution contributes expertise in Chinese social policy and urban governance, enabling robust comparative interpretation.
